results.name: Single Arm Palm Down on Wall Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall and place your palm flat on it behind you at shoulder height, fingers pointing back.
Keep your arm straight.
Slowly turn your body away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Move slowly into the stretch.
Keep your shoulder down.
results.description: Single Arm Palm Down on Wall Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Front Shoulders.

results.name: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch
instructions: Stand beside a wall and place your hand on it at shoulder height with your arm straight.
Rotate your thumb downward.
Turn your body gently away from the wall until you feel a stretch in your biceps.
Hold, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your arm straight.
Breathe steadily.
results.description: Single Arm on Wall Side Biceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Front Shoulders, Chest.

results.name: Standing Adductor Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Keep your hands to your hips.
Shift your weight to your right leg, bending your right knee while keeping your left leg straight. Lean your torso slightly forward.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a stretch along the inner thigh of your left leg.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch on the other side by shifting your weight to your left leg and bending your left knee.
tips: Ensure your bent knee does not extend past your toes to avoid unnecessary strain on the knee joint.
Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
results.description: Standing Adductor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Glutes.

results.name: Standing Bow Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Hinge at your hips and lower your torso towards your legs, reaching your hands towards the back of your feet. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a stretch along the back of your legs.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch as needed.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your weight is distributed evenly on both feet to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your back straight and avoiding excessive rounding of your spine.
results.description: Standing Bow Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back, Glutes.

results.name: Standing Gastrocnemius Stretch
instructions: Stand facing a bench with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Place your right foot on the bench, keeping your heel on the bench and your toes pointing up. Your left foot should remain flat on the floor.
Lean forward slightly, grab your right heel with your right hand, and straighten your leg while lightly pulling your forefoot.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch legs and repeat. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Keep your knees slightly bent to avoid strain or injury of your joints.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
Use a bench at a comfortable height to ensure an effective stretch.
results.description: Standing Gastrocnemius Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Calves, Hamstrings.

results.name: Standing Hamstring Calf Stretch With Resistance Band
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band in both hands. Place the center of the band under your right forefoot.
Extend your right leg straight out in front of you, keeping your heel on the floor and your toes pointing upward. Hold the ends of the resistance band to create tension.
Gently pull on the resistance band, leaning your torso forward to increase the stretch in your right hamstring. Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then switch to your left leg and repeat. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Focus on keeping your extended leg straight and your toes pointing upward.
Ensure your standing leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Use a resistance band with appropriate tension to provide an effective stretch.
results.description: Standing Hamstring Calf Stretch With Resistance Band is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a band, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back, Glutes.

results.name: Standing Lateral Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Place your right hand behind your head. Keep your left hand extended down the side of your leg.
Gently bend your torso to the left as far as possible and hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, feeling a stretch along the right side of your torso.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch on the other side.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Gradually increase the depth of the stretch as your flexibility improves.
Focus on keeping your back straight and avoiding excessive rounding of your spine.
results.description: Standing Lateral Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Core.

results.name: Standing Leg Elevated Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Stand facing an incline bench with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your right heel on the edge of the bench headrest, keeping your leg straight and toes pointing upward.
Engage your core and hinge at your hips, leaning your torso towards your right leg.
Reach towards your right foot with both hands, feeling a stretch along the back of your right leg (hamstring). Hold this position for 20-30 seconds.
Return to the starting position and switch legs. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Focus on keeping your extended leg straight and your toes pointing upward.
Ensure your standing leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Set the bench at an elevated surface at a comfortable height to ensure an effective stretch.
results.description: Standing Leg Elevated Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Lower Back, Glutes.

results.name: Standing One Arm Chest Stretch
instructions: Stand with your right side facing near a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Extend your right arm to the side at shoulder height and place your palm flat against the wall.
Slowly turn your body away from the wall, keeping your arm extended and feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulder.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, maintaining a gentle pressure.
Return to the starting position and repeat the stretch on the left side. Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions on each side.
tips: Focus on keeping your extended arm straight and your palm flat against the wall.
Ensure your shoulders remain relaxed and avoid tensing them up towards your ears.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
results.description: Standing One Arm Chest Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch (Side View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and find a stable surface to hold onto for balance if needed.
Bend your right knee and bring your heel towards your glutes. Grasp your right ankle with your right hand.
Keep your knees close together and lightly pull your right ankle upward, feeling a stretch along the front of your right thigh.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, then release your right ankle and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the left leg.
tips: Perform the stretch slowly and with control to maximize muscle flexibility and reduce injury risk.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Focus on keeping your torso upright and avoid leaning forward or backward.
results.description: Standing Quadriceps Stretch (Side View) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.
